questions.answer: weather, people, language, nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
A lot of bureaucratic and logistics work before the exchange and stressfull finding an apartment, 
but completely worth!!!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Good - BUT a lot of courses on the Griffith webpage appear applicable for everyone, but actually more courses are restricted to only domestic students 
- e.g. if you seek field work within marine science, some courses such as BIODISCOVERY, SCIENCE CAPSTONE is not possible to get even though they don't write it (I found out by mailing the convenor)

questions.answer: Go to orientation week! The people are AMAZING and incredibly helpfull and kind

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
Go to orientation week! The people are AMAZING and incredibly helpfull and kind
sign up for as much as possible

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *

questions.answer: go to Flatmates /Realestates

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
go live in Surfers Paradise or Broadbeach by the beach, it's amazing
and tram is about 0,10 aud only!
some people also lived in Burleigh, but it's pretty far away from the uni

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The friends I met who lived in The Village (the university-provided accommodation) were pretty unhappy with what they got — the prices were very high, some houses had mold, and often 5 people shared a small common space

You can usually find much better options on Flatmates or RealEstate, and you can even live by the beach in Surfers Paradise or Broadbeach!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Alright:)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy to register and apply for the exchange - what took A LOT of time was applying for the expensive student visa (25 pages), applying for funding (make an overview and calendar-based plan here to make it work and do things in good time!) and all the other small things like finding housing, what courses you can take and get merit from etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
some coordinators at KU responsible for exchange to New Zealand and Australia were very helpfull because they answered fast
Griffith uni took more time replying but were also very helpfull when answering the questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I was happy with my courses, and most teachers and classes at Griffith are great!
BUT, as mentioned, it was frustrating that I chose the university partly based on the expectation of taking courses with fieldwork (like MARINE BIODISCOVERY 2803ENV), only to find out one month before the exchange started that some of these courses are for domestic students only — something they don’t mention on the course pages :(

So definitely don’t hesitate to email the course convenors to check whether a class is open to international students as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do everything in as good time as possible, you'll be surprised how long time everything can take and different challenges can occur

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
would've loved to do more field work, but besides that they were great!
also I wish I knew more about the WIL-courses you can take which are similar to PUK-projects! Amazing opportunity to engage in something you're interested in (mail some professors:)
https://www.griffith.edu.au/enrich-your-studies/work-integrated-learning

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Neurobiology – a heavy course that requires quite a bit of time, but very interesting.
Programming Principles – also more time-consuming than expected, but very relevant.
Marine Mammals and Planetary Health – not too hard; interesting content! But some times very unstructured. Unfortunately our (only) dissection class was cancelled last minute. 
Environmental Management – not too hard except for one big assignment, but it requires engagement in voluntary work, which is really cool and a fun way to meet people - and also relevant for future career development.

questions.answer: this is where Griffith is THE BEST

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A LOT of activities and clubs available - they had one (wednes)day after orientation week where many clubs were presented, but they're also listed online (ask StudentGuild)

I joined the uni orchestra, Harmony in Health — honestly the best decision I made. It was amazing socially, culturally, and musically.
My only regret is not joining from the very beginning instead of a month into the trimester.

questions.answer:
pick up and play - sport activities
try the free facilities every friday
go to the cook-up (free dinner) at tuesdays etc.
Trivia night
Orchestra
Hiking club!
Diving club
surfing club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Byron bay, Noosa, Brisbane, if you have a week off then a van trip on the East coast, Fraser island, Whitsundays etc.

And get a car or find some friends with one! then you can go on amazing day-trips to the forrest, Spring brook etc.

You can see glowing worms! Do Mount Tamborine first during daytime (then you educate yourself (e.g. DON'T use iPhone light since it can kill the worms - only RED light!) and you'll know what to look for, really good conservation center) and then do the natural cave in Natural Bridge at evening! Such a beautiful experience not a lot of people know about

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Surfers Paradise has a bit of a superficial, touristy vibe.. like a little Las Vegas.. but uni life is amazing and the system in general is pretty Western

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
sign up for the activities and club(s), ask if people wanna grab lunch after class or coordinate this with some other exchange students, take initiative for weekend/day trips etc.
e.g. Coombabah

and GO TO ORIENTATION WEEK - this is where most exchange students connect

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The superficial vibe of the people in some areas of Surfers paradise (Meriton particularly), found this place on Flatmates

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
the general openness and kindness of people
that people really seek sunrises, sunsets, nature and just good vibes in general
surfing culture was fun to try
A lot of Asian GOOD food in Southport (Southport Library is so nice as well)!

Mostly how amazing the uni was with sooo many social initiatives +
they care a lot about your well-being:) 
LGBT+ friendly, filled with native plants, amazing facilities etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I think sorting out your apartment or housing as soon as possible is important so you can really enjoy the first part of your exchange.

Also, be prepared that the first few weeks (maybe up to 1-1.5 months into the program) can be stressful (don't hold back on calling home to friends/family) - finding people you connect with might take time, and you may try different social groups. Be patient and kind to yourself, stay courageous and curious, and keep attending different social activities (like the hiking club, and don’t be afraid to ask for a lift). Eventually, you’ll find your people ❤️

And remember - it’s totally fine if you’re not into surfing! There’s so much other great stuff to do, especially with all the nature around and other social clubs at uni:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
JUST DO IT:) it will be worth
Gold Coast campus is the best<3

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Friends from all over the world, not just Europeans - Australia is the most international place I've ever been
experiencing the amazing university life and being part of the Uni Orchestra
the beautiful nature that is very close
living by the beach

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: finding a nice and cheap place to live - if possible, live with people from uni (not on campus tho)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Even though it's scary and can be very stressfull the first period, it is VERY rewarding to do and you learn a lot

Remember to take breaks! Taking time for yourself is essential to actually be able to enjoy the time you have there

Don't stay on social media but be present and enjoy the conversations and nature:)
